_about: A year (FY 2025-26) of a 2,000-client programme, as the publication release reads it: the inputs of release-audit.js protectFigures, captured from the benchmark seed (node scripts/bench/run.js --small --seed-only; fictional data, aggregates only). 1.16.0 refused it whole (out of budget); test/publication-release-perf.test.js.

settlement.source_note: Categories follow Exhibit E ("List of Opioid Remediation Uses") of the national opioid settlement agreements and California's High Impact Abatement Activities list, as summarised by DHCS. Both need verification against the agreement governing each fund before the report is submitted; SUDS does not decide whether a cost is allowable.

by_hiaa.label: 1. Matching funds or operating costs for SUD facilities with an approved Behavioral Health Continuum Infrastructure Program (BHCIP) project
2. Creating new or expanded substance use disorder (SUD) treatment infrastructure
3. Addressing the needs of communities of color and vulnerable populations (including sheltered and unsheltered homeless populations) disproportionately impacted by SUD
4. Diversion of people with SUD from the justice system into treatment, including training and resources for first and early responders, and outreach, diversion, deflection and harm reduction
5. Interventions to prevent drug addiction in vulnerable youth
6. The purchase of naloxone for distribution and efforts to expand access to naloxone for opioid overdose reversals
